requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the Rust outline profile meets `requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`. The implementation is complete and marked, the spelling is documented, and the tests cover the main cases and failure paths.

**Implementation**
- `KINDS` in `src/outline/rust.rs` (118–142) maps every item class the requirement lists to a named outline kind:
  - functions and methods (`function_item`, plus `function_signature_item` for trait and extern declarations);
  - `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait`, `mod`, `const`, `static`, and `type` (including `associated_type`);
  - `impl`, `macro` (definitions), and `extern` blocks.
- `impl_name` (7–15) names an impl by the grammar's `type` field plus the optional `trait` field. This gives `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`, and `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` for generics.
- `extern_name` (17–37) names an extern block by its ABI string, or `Rust` when there is none. Rust does not specify a name here, so this choice is documented in `md/reference.md`.
- `use_declaration` and item-position `macro_invocation` are `NameRule::Anonymous`, as the requirement says for items without a suitable name. `item_macro` and `in_item_list` (39–53) restrict macro nodes to item position, so expression macros inside bodies are not nodes.
- Selectors come only from syntactic ancestry within one file, and nothing resolves `mod x;` across files.
- Percent-encoding of names and `#N` disambiguation are done by the shared outline code under `outline_selectors`. The tests exercise both.
- `extern-crate` is an extra kind, but it is documented and within the spirit of the profile.
- Selector spelling is documented in `md/reference.md`: the "References" section (examples such as `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` and `use@…`) and the "Outline profiles" table.
- The `{impl}` markers are on all the relevant code: `impl_name`, `extern_name`, `in_item_list`, `item_macro`, `KINDS`, and `PROFILE`. I found no unmarked code that implements part of the requirement.

**Tests**
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` (`src/outline/tests.rs` 35–100) covers every listed item class:
  - inline and external modules, structs, inherent and trait impls, and an impl on `[u8; 4]` with percent-encoded spelling;
  - trait methods and associated types, `extern "C"` and bare `extern` blocks, nested functions, and `#N` duplicates;
  - macros, unions, enums, consts, statics, type aliases, and `extern crate`.
  - It also checks that selectors resolve back to the right node, that the empty selector is the root, and that an ambiguous or missing selector is an error.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` (619–663) confirms that `use` declarations are anonymous (`use@…`) and distinct.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` (894–927) covers the following:
  - anonymous item macros at top level, in an impl, and in a mod;
  - macros that are not nodes inside function bodies;
  - the generic impl name `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.

**Remaining gaps**
Minor edge cases are untested, such as foreign types and raw-string ABIs. They are not specified behavior and do not undermine the requirement.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
